legacy_cells.B: Quantifying uncertainty in microbiome-based prediction using Gaussian processes with microbial community dissimilarities
legacy_cells.C: Asahi Adachi; Fan Zhang; Shigehiko Kanaya; Naoaki Ono
legacy_cells.I: 074_2024_Quantifying uncertainty in microbiome-based prediction using Gaussian processes with microbial community dissimilarities.pdf
legacy_cells.O: Human gut microbiome-based prediction of chronological age, body mass index (BMI), and Crohn’s disease severity (CDAI)
legacy_cells.S: Can human gut microbial abundance data predict chronological age, BMI, and Crohn’s disease severity (CDAI)?
legacy_cells.AI: 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing-derived human gut microbial community abundance (OTU/ASV relative abundances)
legacy_cells.CR: Confidence-interval calibration evaluated by empirical coverage and expected calibration error (ECE); confidence curves related uncertainty to prediction error.
legacy_cells.FL: Relative-abundance OTU/ASV inputs are compared using microbial dissimilarity measures; single or summed dissimilarity-based kernels feed GP regression, which outputs predictive distributions for age, BMI, or CDAI. No temporal transition or planner is implemented.
legacy_cells.FM: Develops GP kernel functions incorporating microbial community dissimilarities, including a multiple-kernel function, for probabilistic prediction and uncertainty quantification from microbiome data.
legacy_cells.FN: The multiple-kernel GP achieved NLL 3.80 ± 0.01 for age, 2.34 ± 0.00 for BMI, and 3.43 ± 0.04 for CDAI; results report close agreement between confidence and empirical coverage.
legacy_cells.FO: The authors identify exact-GP scalability limitations: time complexity O(N³) and storage requirement O(N²), challenging for large-scale microbiome datasets.
legacy_cells.FP: Future work should explore sparse GP variants for scalability and the method’s potential for daily health monitoring and early disease detection.
legacy_cells.FQ: The authors state that uncertainty quantification in microbiome-based prediction models remained unexplored.
legacy_cells.FR: Evidence boundary: experiments are retrospective, repeated 50/50 train/test regressions on microbiome cohorts. They evaluate predictive accuracy and uncertainty, not evolving patient states, action-conditioned rollouts, identified treatment effects, planning, or prospective clinical utility; clinical application is proposed rather than tested.
legacy_cells.FS: Reviewer mapping: M7 Outcome & causal layer; M9 Safety & governance
legacy_cells.FT: Reviewer lesson: Preserve predictive uncertainty when routing clinical estimates to the safety layer; calibration must be retested after coupling to dynamics.
legacy_cells.FX: Title and abstract (PDF p. 1); Introduction (pp. 1–2); Methods §§2.1–2.5 and Table 1 (pp. 2–4); Results §§3.1–3.3, Tables 2–3 and Figures 1–3 (pp. 4–6); Discussion, limitations, Conclusion, and availability/statements (pp. 6–8); references and final publication page (pp. 8–9). | Codex audit: title/byline, abstract/conclusion, targeted methods/results and cross-check of prior quotations against extracted full text. This is a targeted audit, not an independent re-extraction of every negative/unreported field.
legacy_cells.FZ: A:I left unchanged. The paper evaluates static supervised regression on microbiome data and has no demonstrated temporal state transition, action conditioning, rollout, planner, or agent. The extracted Table 1 text has misaligned row/column values, so sample counts were omitted. No external sources or systems were used. Evidence QA: 12/41 populated fields had a <=25-word quotation matching extracted PDF text (29.3%). Confidence is conservative; review this row where exact quote checks were incomplete. Codex audit: 38 prior populated fields have a located source quotation; 3 have quotations not located by normalized text matching. Unlocated quotations are review flags, not proof that the value is false. Companion evidence audit lists affected columns. Reviewer FS/FT/FU mappings are synthesis. Prior unsupported/missing fields remain Not reported; no clinical benefit inferred from offline simulation.
